It’s Official: Timekeepers Have Gotten Rid of the Leap Second—and Introduced the Leap Hour Instead
https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/its-official-timek…
Every four years, February gets an extra day. You’ve heard of these “leap” years, especially if an acquaintance was born on the unusual date of February 29. What you might not have heard of, however, is the leap year’s sporadic sibling: the leap second.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leap_second
In October 2026, the leap second was officially abolished. This decision was enacted by a vote of representatives at a meeting of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) in Versailles, France. 1

[whyisave] @fantombloo: I don't know what counterpoint are you offering, because I'm already in agreement with you.
My initial comment is to remind the commenter, that the current Gregorian calendar is inherently a "Christian calendar' by the virtue of those who were responsible on developing that calendar.
There's a smiley emoji at the end of another sentence, to reflect the sentiment behind that specific statement preceding the emoji.
Then, I proceeded to say that there is another view, which places the earth at the 'centre' of observable satellite objects, such as the moon, hence the development of the lunar calendar.
I repeat this, in the next comment, which is still saying that there are those that place the sun the centre of their calendar, and then there are others who place the earth at the centre of their calendar.
These are 2 concurrent and valid views, according to their disciples.
Then, I add that solar calendars were also important for agrarian societies in the northern hemisphere, because their spring-time is the time of celebrations, based around when seeds are planted, eg. look at Persian New Year, Indian New Year, etc… are all celebrated around the same time of the year.
